value.rationale: Opposite-part isolate counts measure two essential deficiencies of incidence matrices and bipartite network samples; the exact model-sensitive sign transition at fixed matched edge intensity matters for inference and matching-coverage regimes. Strict finite classification and a nonzero negative sparse constant quantify genuinely different second-order behavior; Bernoulli covariance is order n positive and with-replacement exactly zero. This is a natural two-class covariance, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
